_comment: Tool servers both agents can reach. ONE file, two dialects:
- OpenCode gets the 'mcp' block of opencode.json, on `bin/flora render`
- Hermes gets `hermes mcp add ...`, on `bin/flora sync`
Add a server here and run `bin/flora sync`; never edit either agent's
config directly, or they will drift.
${VAR} is expanded from the environment at render time, so credentials stay
in secrets/flora.env and never land in a tracked file.
Set "enabled": false to keep a definition around without loading it.

atlassian.note: Confluence and Jira through Atlassian's own MCP server. Enable it and run `bin/flora sync`, then complete the OAuth flow once with: bin/flora hermes mcp login atlassian

filesystem.note: Both agents already have shell access to workspace/, so this is usually redundant. Useful if you tighten the shell tool later.
